questions.questionText: hour 15 minutes Additional Materials: Multiple Choice Answer Sheet Soft clean eraser Soft pencil (type B or HB is recommended) READ THESE INSTRUCTIONS FIRST Write in soft pencil. Do not use staples, paper clips, glue or correction fluid. Write your name, Centre number and candidate number on the Answer Sheet in the spaces provided unless this has been done for you. DO NOT WRITE IN ANY BARCODES. There are thirty questions on this paper. Answer all questions. For each question there are four possible answers A, B, C and D. Choose the one you consider correct and record your choice in soft pencil on the separate Answer Sheet. Read the instructions on the Answer Sheet very carefully. Each correct answer will score one mark. A mark will not be deducted for a wrong answer. Any rough working should be done in this booklet.
What is a negative externality from consumption?

options.A: a new road that results in more sales at shops in the town centre
options.B: a successful promotion of healthy eating that reduces days lost from work
options.C: discharge of waste from a factory that damages fish in a local river
options.D: increased popularity of smoking that increases demand on the health service

questions.questionText: Which type of efficiency is identified by price = marginal cost?

options.D: technical

questions.questionText: A consumer can purchase two goods, X and Y, from a given income. What will cause the consumer’s budget line to make a parallel shift to the right? consumer’s income price of good X price of good Y

options.D: 10% increase 20% increase 20% increase

questions.questionText: The line RS in the diagram shows the different combinations of goods X and Y that a consumer can afford with her present income. quantity R of Y N M S O quantity of X The consumer’s original equilibrium is at M. What could explain a subsequent change in her equilibrium position to N?

options.B: an increase in the price of X and a fall in the price of Y
options.C: an increase in the price of X and a smaller percentage increase in the price of Y
options.D: equal percentage increases in her income and in both prices

questions.questionText: The table shows the total revenue and marginal cost of a firm at different levels of production. production total marginal (tonnes) revenue ($) cost ($)
240 Within which output range will the firm’s profits be maximised?

options.D: 6–7 tonnes

questions.questionText: What must be different between the consumers of a product to enable profitable price discrimination by the producer?

options.D: time of consumption

questions.questionText: An example of forward vertical integration for a computer manufacturer would be a merger with

options.D: a software developer.

A cartel has been successful in regulating output. However, recently it has shown signs of breaking up. Which feature of the market could have caused this?

options.A: an agreement that the cartel produces a homogenous product
options.B: an increase in the number of small, independent producers of the good
options.C: stable patterns of demand for the good
options.D: trademarks, acting as a barrier to entry to the market

questions.questionText: What would be most likely to allow the survival of small firms in an economy?

options.A: an increase in the cost of borrowing from commercial banks
options.B: an increase in personal services as a share of GDP
options.C: an increase in the rate of change of information technology
options.D: an increase in the ratio of capital to labour employed in an economy

questions.questionText: A private company operates a coal mine which employs 400 workers. The mining operations have polluted the environment and created external costs. If the government intervenes, how could it internalise the externality?

options.A: close part of the mine and import the coal
options.B: levy an additional tax on the miners’ wages equal to the external cost
options.C: pay for the external costs of restoring the environment after mining
options.D: place a tax equivalent to the external cost on the output the company produces

questions.questionText: What is an advantage of using tradable pollution permits to control pollution?

options.A: Tradable permits are restricted to the firms to which they are issued.
options.C: Tradable permits encourage the use of market forces.
options.D: Tradable permits guarantee a zero level of pollution.

questions.questionText: Where might government intervention to raise the wages of a group of workers be justified in order to prevent their exploitation?

options.A: in an industry that is protected by tariffs on imports from abroad
options.B: in an industry when a trade union negotiates wages for the workers
options.C: in an industry when the output is produced by a single firm monopolist
options.D: in an industry when workers are employed by a monopsonist

questions.questionText: There is a decrease in the supply of female labour. What will be the likely effect on male and female wages? male wages female wages

options.D: increase increase

questions.questionText: Which criteria are used in official labour market surveys to determine whether a person should be classified as being unemployed? eligible for receipt actively seeking available to of unemployment employment at the start work benefit current wage rate

options.D: yes no yes

questions.questionText: To increase the number of cleaners at a local school from 10 to 11, the employer has to raise the hourly rate of pay from $3.00 to $3.25. What is the marginal cost of labour per hour to the employer?
What would result in a reduction in labour costs per unit of output?

options.A: an increase in average earnings which is less than the increase in employment
options.B: an increase in labour productivity which is less than the increase in average earnings
options.C: an increase in output which is greater than the increase in labour earnings
options.D: an increase in wage rates which is greater than the increase in output per worker

questions.questionText: Out of any addition to national income, 25% is spent on imports, 15% is paid in taxes, 10% is saved and the rest is spent on domestically produced goods. What is the value of the multiplier?
Which economic indicator uses the following three components to obtain a value between 0 (low) and 1 (high)? ● GNI per capita ● life expectancy ● education

options.D: Measure of Economic Welfare

questions.questionText: What is not a possible benefit to a developing country of a multinational company investing in a new factory in that country?

options.C: extra tax revenue for the government
options.D: increased competition for small domestic producers

questions.questionText: Which policy is best to reduce cyclical unemployment?

options.D: reduce the money supply

questions.questionText: A government decided to increase its expenditure on a major infrastructure project by building new roads. What would decrease the multiplier effect of the project if it had occurred at the same time?

options.B: a decrease in the rate of interest
options.D: an increase in the marginal propensity to consume

questions.questionText: A country is in recession with unused resources. The government reduces interest rates. What do Keynesian economists believe the short-run outcome will be? unemployment economic growth inflation

options.D: increase unchanged uncertain

When will an inflationary gap exist in an economy?

options.A: when aggregate demand is greater than full employment income
options.B: when leakages exceed injections at the full employment income
options.C: when money wage rises exceed rises in labour productivity
options.D: when the money supply rises faster than nominal national income

questions.questionText: What is the basic assumption underlying the accelerator theory?

options.A: Investment depends on the level of business confidence.
options.B: Investment depends on the level of savings.
options.C: Investment depends on the rate of change in consumer demand.
options.D: Investment depends on the rate of change of interest rates.
